items.stem: ‘Sharpeville was the turning point in resistance to apartheid.’ How far do you agree?
items.answer: For: It led to the banning of the ANC and PAC. It led the ANC to turn to armed struggle. It brought international condemnation. items.stem: Study Sources C and D. Source C: Nelson Mandela, statement from the dock at the Rivonia Trial, April 1964 (abridged). “I have cherished the ideal of a democratic and free society in which all persons live together in harmony and with equal opportunities. It is an ideal which I hope to live for and to achieve. But if needs be, it is an ideal for which I am prepared to die.” Source D: a report by a foreign journalist, 1976 (illustrative). “The students marched singing, carrying placards. When the police fired, the protest spread across the township and then the country. Something has changed: the young are no longer afraid.” Identify one similarity and one difference between Sources C and D on apartheid and resistance.
items.answer: Source C: Mandela states his commitment to a democratic, non-racial society. Source D: It suggests Soweto marked a new phase of mass resistance. A similarity and a difference must each be supported by details from both sources.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a similarity and 1 for supporting it from both sources; 1 mark for a difference and 1 for supporting it from both sources [4]

items.stem: ‘Sharpeville was the turning point in resistance to apartheid.’ Discuss.
items.answer: For: It led to the banning of the ANC and PAC. It led the ANC to turn to armed struggle. It brought international condemnation. Against: Resistance was crushed for over a decade afterwards. Soweto in 1976 revived mass resistance. The 1980s township revolt and the UDF did more to weaken apartheid. Judgement: Sharpeville changed the methods of resistance, but Soweto marked the real revival of mass opposition.

items.stem: P. W. Botha became prime minister in 1978. Analyse the reasons why Botha's Total Strategy failed.
items.answer: Reforms were too limited and provoked resistance, as with the Tricameral Parliament. The UDF and township revolt made areas ungovernable. International sanctions and disinvestment damaged the economy. The cost of military action in Angola and the region. Botha's refusal to share power with the Black majority. Judgement: reform without power-sharing satisfied no one, provoking internal resistance that repression and the economy could not contain.

items.stem: Put these events in chronological order, starting with the earliest. A: De Klerk became president. B: Chris Hani was assassinated. C: The ANC was unbanned. D: The first democratic elections were held.

items.stem: How far was apartheid a continuation of earlier segregation?
items.answer: For: Land segregation dated from 1913. Pass laws and job reservation existed before 1948. Black Africans already lacked political rights in most areas. Against: Apartheid was more systematic and ideological. It classified the whole population by race. It removed the remaining rights of Coloured voters. Judgement: apartheid built on earlier segregation, but its systematic racial classification made it a new and harsher system.

items.stem: Source C is a South African businessman, 1989 (illustrative). “Sanctions, strikes and the falling rand are bleeding us dry. Business can no longer live with apartheid; we have told the government so.” Study the source. Assess the reliability of Source C as evidence about economic pressures.
items.answer: Reliable because it shows business opinion. Less reliable because business leaders had their own interests. Cross-reference: It does not show de Klerk's motives. Judgement: reliable as evidence of this point of view, but it needs to be tested against other evidence.

items.stem: Source C is F. W. de Klerk, speech at the opening of parliament, 2 February 1990 (summary). De Klerk announced the unbanning of the ANC, PAC and Communist Party and the release of political prisoners, and called for negotiations on a new constitution. Study the source. Assess the reliability of Source C as evidence about the end of apartheid.
items.answer: Reliable because it is the president's own announcement. Less reliable because it presented the decision as his initiative, not as a response to pressure. Cross-reference: It does not show the pressures that led to it. Judgement: reliable as evidence of this point of view, but it needs to be tested against other evidence.
